content.title: Is Your Child Losing Their Character While Chasing Success?
content.subtitle: The anguish of a generation at risk and a humble appeal to parents.
content.body:
In May 2023, during a special police raid on residential hotels in Dhaka’s Farmgate area, dozens of young men and women were detained. Among their belongings, police found physics notebooks and ID cards from well-known colleges. The girl cried with her face covered by her scarf, while the boy trembled as he looked at the handcuffs.

In February 2024, several students from renowned private universities were detained from a flat in Uttara over immoral activities and drug use. They had rented the apartment under the pretext of studying but had become immersed in a live-in relationship culture.

The Cruel Trap of Becoming ‘Established’

Today, our society has turned marriage from a blessed act of worship into a difficult social test. As soon as a young man turns twenty or twenty-two, a mountain of conditions stands before him: finish your studies, pass the BCS examination, own a flat and a car, and build substantial savings. Until he becomes financially established, marriage is barely considered an option.

But does anyone notice how young people gradually wear themselves down while struggling against their nafs throughout ten to twelve years of youth? When the lid of a boiling pot is held shut, the steam will eventually burst through it. In an age when haram is available at the click of a button, is it easy to remain chaste until thirty, thirty-two, or thirty-five? Many young people eventually achieve worldly success, but their spiritual and moral purity may already have suffered along the way.

What Is the Worth of Success Without Character?

Wanting a bright future for your child is not wrong. But every parent should ask: if your child becomes a BCS cadre or a senior officer, yet secretly earns their Lord’s displeasure and loses their chastity and modesty along the way, what is that success truly worth?

Can there be genuine peace in an achievement that leaves a person spiritually empty and without Taqwa? What is the point of earning a worldly title if it brings no benefit in the Hereafter?

The Simple Path Taught by the Prophet ﷺ

More than fourteen hundred years ago, our beloved Prophet ﷺ understood this human struggle and offered a clear solution. Addressing the youth, he said:

“O young people! Whoever among you is able to marry should marry, for it helps lower the gaze and guard one's chastity...” (Sahih al-Bukhari: 5066)

The Prophet ﷺ never demanded that someone become extremely wealthy or powerful before marriage. Rather, he encouraged marriage when a person had the basic ability to take responsibility, helping them establish a pure life. He also advised guardians:

“When someone whose religious commitment and character please you comes to you with a marriage proposal, then marry him. If you do not, there will be tribulation and widespread corruption on earth.” (Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi: 1084)

Isn’t today’s moral decline and the growing misguidance of our children a reflection of this warning?

A Heartfelt Appeal to Parents: Make Marriage Easier

Let go of the unrealistic idea that every child must become a doctor or a BCS cadre. When your child reaches adulthood and has the basic means to earn a halal living, do not delay marriage unnecessarily. Your child’s Iman and moral purity are far more valuable than society’s judgment.

Allah says in the Holy Qur’an:

“Marry off those among you who are unmarried... If they are poor, Allah will enrich them through His grace.” (Surah An-Nur: 32)

Trust Allah’s promise. Remove unnecessary ceremonial expenses and excessive conditions, and make marriage easier for your children. Try to understand their loneliness and inner struggles. Help them build a halal home that protects their Iman and allows them to become a source of comfort and joy for you in this world and the Hereafter.
